summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Skyline through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating options for hosted vs dedicated for latency-sensitive chat and embeddings at scale. Key concerns: token-level costs, per-route attribution, SSO/KMS integration, and ability to run a short POC with deterministic benchmarking.
transcript: 00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Samir's here from our solutions engineering team. 00:08 Maya Raju: Hi Alex, hey Samir, thanks — we have Jon and Priya joining as well. quick note, i'm on east coast, bit of background: we run a large recommendation chat feature and embeddings for search, and cost is our top blocker. 00:22 Samir Patel: great, totally — today we'll focus on the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown so you can see token-level attribution and route-level metrics. 00:33 Jon Keller: sounds good, want to see how we can map to our existing Grafana stack too, and whether we can get per-model, per-route latency SLOs. 00:42 Samir Patel: yeah, we have the per-route dashboards that show request rate, p50/p95 latency, tokens in/out, and cost burn by route and by model. i'll share my screen, bear with me while the deck loads. 01:05 Samir Patel: (screen shares) here is the usage analytics home, you can filter by route name, model family, and time window. this is a common source of confusion — routes map to your api endpoints, so you get direct correlation with product features. 01:28 Maya Raju: that mapping will be super helpful — we have 12 routes right now, some are chat with long context, others are short completion calls for snippets. how does cost get attributed for long context calls, like our chat with a 4k context? 01:42 Samir Patel: good q — Console shows tokens consumed for request and response separately, and cost is computed using model-unit rates. for long contexts we show a rolling KV cache hit rate as well — you can see how much prefix caching is reducing net token spend. 02:00 Priya Singh: oh nice — is KV cache visible per-tenant or per-route? because we have a mix of anonymous traffic and logged-in users, want to understand cache effectiveness. 02:12 Samir Patel: it's per-route and per-session granularity where we can, depends on whether you're on hosted or dedicated; for hosted we show aggregate cache hit for the route, for dedicated you can enable more detailed traces. 02:29 Jon Keller: dedicated vs hosted — we're leaning toward dedicated for predictable latency, but worried about unit cost. can you show how Redwood estimates cost for dedicated pools vs hosted per-token billing? 02:43 Samir Patel: sure — on the cost breakdown page we have two views: usage-based burn (hosted) which multiplies tokens by model rate, and reserved-capacity amortized cost (dedicated) which shows burn rate across committed GPU hours + spot/burst adjustments. you can compare apples-to-apples: tokens normalized to per-1M requests or per-100k tokens. 03:05 Alex Chen: additionally, the Console includes a cost-simulator where you can toggle batching levels, KV cache hit improvement, and quantization profile to see the estimated monthly spend impact. 03:18 Maya Raju: there was a mention in your docs about model variants & automated fallback. how does that appear in the console? 03:26 Samir Patel: we have rollout panels — you can define a primary model and fallback variants; the dashboard shows traffic split, quality metrics (custom evals) and the cost delta. it's useful for canarying a cheaper quantized variant while monitoring regressions. 03:46 Priya Singh: quality metrics — can we hook our existing evals? we run unit prompt sets against different models to detect regressions. 03:53 Samir Patel: yeah, we support uploading eval prompt sets or integrating with your CI. the console surfaces regression alerts tied to prompt sets so if a cheaper quantized model drops accuracy on those prompts we flag it. 04:10 Jon Keller: on security, our security team wants SOC2, SSO with SAML, customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. how do those show up in the console? 04:21 Alex Chen: good — we have audit logs and role-based access in the console; SSO/SAML is supported at the workspace level. KMS integration exists and for Private deployments you can bring your own key material. VPC peering and private control plane are part of our Private offering. i'll add our security pack doc to the follow ups. 04:38 Maya Raju: perfect. also, how granular is the cost attribution if a single UX action hits multiple routes (e.g., search triggers embedding + rerank)? 04:50 Samir Patel: we provide per-route tracing that tags a parent request id so you can roll up costs to a single customer journey. there can be small attribution edges with third-party preprocessing but we surface the lineage. 05:05 Priya Singh: can we export the raw per-token billing table? our finance team wants the CSV for chargeback. 05:12 Samir Patel: yes exportable, and you can push to S3 daily. we also have an API for programmatic export if you want to ingest into your billing pipeline. 05:21 Jon Keller: any built-in anomaly detection? last month we had a spike from a runaway loop. 05:28 Samir Patel: Console has threshold-based alerts and model-behavior anomaly detection that flags unusual token burn or latency spikes, with links to sampled requests to help debugging. 05:40 Maya Raju: okay useful. for the POC we want to run a synthetic benchmark that mirrors our production mix — can you run that or do we run it? 05:49 Alex Chen: we usually provide a benchmark harness and run jointly. Samir will share the checklist and a sample workload; we can also run a Redwood-managed run against hosted endpoints or a dedicated test pool. 06:02 Samir Patel: i'll also include guidance on kernel/quantization profiles to try. note that perf numbers vary by sequence distribution and batching strategy. 06:15 Priya Singh: about per-route dashboards — can I create custom computed metrics? e.g. cost per successful recommendation conversion. 06:23 Samir Patel: yep you can define custom metrics and derived dashboards; they can be persisted and scheduled reports emailed to stakeholders. 06:34 Jon Keller: curious about long-term retention for analytics — how long do you keep request-level logs? 06:40 Alex Chen: default is 90 days at the plan level, enterprise add-on for extended retention and raw logs archival. retention is configurable per-account. 06:52 Maya Raju: fine, what about redaction? PII in prompts, we need to ensure masked tokens don't leave our environment. 06:58 Samir Patel: we have prompt/response redaction options and configurable retention; for Private deployments you can set no remote retention and have local logging only. 07:12 Priya Singh: any friction integrating with our existing observability (Datadog/Grafana)? 07:18 Samir Patel: we provide exported metrics, logs and tracing hooks; Datadog/Grafana dashboards are supported via exporters. 07:26 Maya Raju: can you show the cost simulator for a concrete example — let's say our chat route sees 10k QPS peak with average 800 tokens per session and embeddings route at 500 QPS with 128 token average. 07:40 Samir Patel: sure, toggling parameters now — baseline hosted with model A at $0.xx per 1k tokens yields estimated $Xk/month. enabling batch size 8 drops estimated cost by ~18%, enabling KV cache at 30% hit saves another 12%. switching to quantized variant reduces compute by approx 30% but we flagged slight eval regression on some prompts — you'll see that in the rollout quality pane. 08:12 Jon Keller: those are promising numbers. how does the console present cost per tenant vs global? 08:19 Samir Patel: per-tenant breakdown is enabled with tenant tagging; you can see per-tenant monthly spend and set quotas and alerts. for chargeback we recommend the CSV export. 08:31 Maya Raju: ok, last part — SLA and fallbacks; what happens if a dedicated pool loses capacity? 08:40 Alex Chen: we have routing policies, you can define fallback to hosted or to a cheaper availability tier. Console shows the fallback chain and historical failover events. 08:52 Priya Singh: one small practical question — will we get sample dashboards as JSON or something to import? 08:58 Samir Patel: yes, dashboard templates are exportable/importable JSON. i'll attach the template to the follow up. 09:05 Maya Raju: thank you — this was helpful. recap for us: we'd like the pricing, benchmark harness, and to schedule a POC kickoff. 09:14 Alex Chen: great, i'll send the pricing + SOW template, Samir will send the benchmark and dashboard templates. i'll propose POC kickoff times for the week of 8/31. 09:22 Jon Keller: thanks everyone, Priya and I will validate routes and send sample route configs. 09:28 Alex Chen: awesome, we'll follow up; appreciate your time.
